speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing difficulty conceiving and discomfort during sexual activity. To begin our evaluation, have you noticed any pain specifically during penetration, and has this been happening for more than three months?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vulvodynia secondary to pelvic floor dysfunction.

Based on your history of 15 months of infertility, the husband's occasional erectile difficulties, and specifically your reported pelvic floor muscle tension during penetration, I suspect this pain is a primary cause of the dyspareunia. Given the diagnosis of body dysmorphic disorder, there may also be a psychosomatic component contributing to your symptoms. Can you describe the exact location of your pain and whether it is constant or only triggered by touch?
